commit.message:
Refresh README: verified API accuracy, simplified diagram, restored content (#2)

- Fixed 4 API-reference member claims that lumped sibling classes
  together as if they shared an identical method set, checked against
  the real TypeScript source: Vector2/Vector3/Vector4 (only Vector3 has
  dot/cross/normalize), FVector2/FVector3/FVector4 (only FVector2 has
  arithmetic add/sub/mul/div; FVector4 is field-accessors-only),
  BoundingBox/BoundingBox2D/BoundingBoxExtent (BoundingBox2D has no
  contains; BoundingBoxExtent has none of merge/contains/overlapsWith),
  and a missing ThreeMfLoadOptions.flipCoordinateSystem entry.
- Rewrote the 2 GltfExporter runtime-defect descriptions (the binary
  glTF RangeError, the node-hierarchy round-trip issue) and the
  adm-zip packaging note down to plain, non-forensic pointers to
  upstream-issues.md, removing internal implementation detail
  (buffer-sizing internals, exact exception text) from the README
  itself.
- Restructured Scope and Limitations into a bulleted list; the
  Enterprise Edition paragraph now names the specific capabilities
  gained (rendering, additional exchange formats, full production
  feature completeness).
- Simplified the At a Glance diagram to Starting Points -> Product ->
  Core Capabilities -> Outputs.
- Restored a real, verified link to AGENTS.md (contributor guide) that
  a previous refresh pass had dropped.
- Collapsed the full test/type-check command list into a <details>
  block under Development and Testing, keeping install/build visible.
- Added the project's banner image and title-cased every heading.

Verification: every code example and every API Reference member claim
was checked against the real compiled TypeScript source
(tsc --strict plus direct source inspection); the diagram's format
claims were checked against both this knowledge base's format data
and the real source, not either alone.

Co-authored-by: babar-raza <babar-raza@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

repo.description: Aspose.3D FOSS for TypeScript is a MIT-licensed library for working with 3D file formats in Node.js applications. Install it with a single npm install @aspose/3d command and start reading, constructing, and writing 3D scenes in TypeScript immediately, with no native addons to compile, no external SDKs to install, and no renderer required.
repo.name: Aspose.3D-FOSS-for-TypeScript
